hints: Consider the horizontal forces acting on the trailing truck alone.
Since the truck moves at constant speed ($a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}$) and experiences no resistance, apply Newton's second law to find the tension.
walkthrough:
Focus on the trailing truck of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$. Name Newton's second law of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$

Identify the horizontal forces acting on the truck. The forward pulling force is the coupling tension $T$, and the problem states that there is no resistance force acting on the truck ($R_{\text{truck}} = 0\text{ N}$):
$$F_{\text{net}} = T - 0 = T$$

Because the system moves at a constant speed of $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$T = (0.4)(0) = 0\text{ N}$$

hints: Determine the driving force at constant speed, which must balance the total resistance of 0.2 N.
Use the power formula $P = Fv$ with driving force $F = 0.2\text{ N}$ and speed $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Name the foundational formula relating power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = Fv$$

At constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force $F$ produced by the locomotive engine must equal the total resistance opposing motion:
$$F = R_{\text{locomotive}} + R_{\text{truck}} = 0.2 + 0 = 0.2\text{ N}$$

Substitute the driving force $F = 0.2\text{ N}$ and constant speed $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the power equation:
$$P = (0.2)(2) = 0.4\text{ W}$$

hints: Calculate the new driving force at the instant power increases to 1.2 W using $F = \dfrac{P}{v}$ with current speed $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the whole connected system (mass 1.2 kg) to find the acceleration $a$.
Apply Newton's second law to the truck alone ($T = m_{\text{truck}} a$) to determine the tension in the coupling.
walkthrough:
State the relationship between driving force $F$, engine power $P$, and instantaneous speed $v$:
$$F = \frac{P}{v}$$

At the instant the power changes to $1.2\text{ W}$, the speed of the train is still $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the new driving force:
$$F = \frac{1.2}{2} = 0.6\text{ N}$$

Name Newton's second law of motion for the entire train (locomotive plus truck as a single unit):
$$F_{\text{net}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$

Add the masses and equate net forward force (driving force minus resistance) to total mass times acceleration:
$$m_{\text{total}} = 0.8 + 0.4 = 1.2\text{ kg}$$
$$0.6 - 0.2 = 1.2a$$
$$0.4 = 1.2a$$

Divide both sides by 1.2 to find the common acceleration:
$$a = \frac{0.4}{1.2} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the truck of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ alone, where the only horizontal force is the coupling tension $T$:
$$T = m_{\text{truck}} a$$

Substitute $m_{\text{truck}} = 0.4\text{ kg}$ and $a = \frac{1}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T = (0.4)\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{4}{10} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{30} = \frac{2}{15}\text{ N}\quad (\approx 0.133\text{ N})$$
